unique_findings: They treat time as the primary signal and position as a derived product — the core engineering emphasis is sub-nanosecond phase/time synchronization across existing RAN elements and Wi‑Fi APs, rather than inventing new ranging signals or device-side clients.

Use of SRS (uplink sounding reference signals) instead of PRS/PRS-like dedicated positioning signals is an unusual choice: SRS is high-rate (~100–500 Hz) and mandatory for connectivity, enabling continuous tracking without handset consent, but extracting reliable ranging from SRS requires coherent, phase-stable capture at the network side.

Claims of sub-10cm accuracy using only 10–20 MHz of bandwidth and ranges to 1.5 km point to phase-based carrier measurements (carrier-phase TDoA / phase-differencing) rather than classical wideband time-of-flight. That implies they are doing carrier-phase ambiguity resolution, continuous phase tracking, and network-level cycle-slip mitigation.

Network-side deployment without device changes implies deep integration/taps into baseband / radio units or virtualized RAN (vRAN) stacks to access raw SRS/CSI streams and per-antenna phase information — not just OTAs or packet timestamps. This is an operational and engineering departure from server-side fingerprinting approaches.

Their architecture appears to centralize 'movement ledger' creation: a continuous, time-synchronized spatial database fed by many heterogeneous radios (5G, Wi‑Fi, LoRa). This is a product+data moat: the time-aligned multi-modal stream is more valuable than isolated position fixes.

To achieve sub-ns synchronization across distributed receivers without adding GNSS on every node, they likely use a hybrid of fiber/ptp with phase calibration, over-the-air reciprocity, and algorithmic clock-offset estimation using multi-site observations — a mix rarely commercialized at scale.

Marketing claims gloss over the hardest problems: multipath/NLOS, antenna array calibration and per-device antenna biases, dynamic carrier-phase ambiguities, asymmetric RF chains, and varying front-end latencies across vendor equipment — all of which explode complexity as you scale.

The solution is protocol-agnostic in marketing, but practically it depends on getting deterministic, low-jitter access to physical-layer observables (phase, CSI, timestamps) — this requires vendor/operator cooperation (RAN OEMs, vRAN hooks, or RF taps) and bespoke integration per deployment.

competitors.similarity: Control device-side location stacks, manage OS-level privacy/permissions, and provide positioning frameworks for apps.
competitors.how_different: ZaiNar explicitly bypasses handset gatekeepers by using network-emitted connectivity signals (SRS) so carriers can obtain positioning independent of OS permissions; Google/Apple control device-side access and often limit network-side positioning signals like PRS.

differentiation.primary: Network-side sub-nanosecond time synchronization that uses existing connectivity signals (SRS) to produce continuous, carrier-scalable, sub-meter to sub-10cm positioning without device changes or battery impact.
differentiation.technical: Phase-based, sub-nanosecond time synchronization and distribution across wireless networks; ingestion and processing of raw high-rate connectivity signals (SRS) instead of low-rate PRS/PRS-type signals; protocol-agnostic engine that works across 5G, WiFi, LoRa; low-bandwidth operation (claimed on as little as 10–20 MHz); centralized, low-latency APIs and event streams delivering real-time coordinates and motion intelligence.
differentiation.business: Go-to-market focused on carriers, OEMs, and system integrators to convert existing infrastructure into a monetizable spatial service; no reliance on device OEM cooperation or apps lowers friction and enables direct telco-enterprise monetization; emphasis on SLA-grade, enterprise APIs and event streams for Physical AI customers.
differentiation.positioning: Positions itself as the foundational 'Physical AI' spatial layer and the '5G killer app' that turns networks into sensing infrastructure — framing competitors as limited (PRS, GPS, UWB, cameras, fingerprinting) and ZaiNar as the only solution that provides continuous, centralized, sub-ns-synced spatial data at scale without additional hardware or battery cost.

secret_sauce.core_advantage: Patented, phase-based sub-nanosecond time synchronization and the ability to extract high-precision spatial information from existing high-rate connectivity signals (SRS) across deployed networks — enabling network-side positioning at scales, ranges, and accuracies that competitors (which depend on PRS, dedicated anchors, GNSS, or device-side cooperation) cannot match.
secret_sauce.defensibility: Large patent portfolio (100+ filed, ~90 issued claimed), carrier integrations and commercial contracts, engineering difficulty of achieving and distributing sub-nanosecond synchronization across heterogeneous network elements, and the strategic advantage of operating as a network-side SaaS/platform that requires access to operator infrastructure (which creates non-trivial commercial and technical integration barriers).

“ZaiNar's patented technology uses the connectivity signals (SRS) that every device already transmits... SRS signals are transmitted 100 to 500 times per second, enabling ZaiNar to track fast-moving objects...”

competitive_analysis.moat_explanation: ZaiNar combines deep technical innovation (claimed sub-nanosecond phase-based synchronization), a large patent portfolio, and the go-to-market lever of carrier integration — all of which create meaningful barriers to entry. However, the moat is not unassailable: major telco vendors, chipset makers, or large cloud/network players could attempt to replicate or integrate similar capabilities (especially if standards or operator demand evolve). Regulatory, privacy, and operator-commercial dynamics also determine access to the necessary raw SRS data; if operators prefer other partners or standards bodies codify alternate methods, competitive pressures could increase. Therefore the advantage is defensible today but requires continued IP, deployment scale, and operator partnerships to remain robust.

evidence_quotes: Network-as-sensor paradigm: using existing connectivity signals (SRS) required for connectivity rather than dedicated PRS/PRS-like signals or extra hardware on devices.
Sub-nanosecond, phase-based time synchronization and distribution across existing wireless infrastructure to derive centimeter-/sub-meter-level positioning without device-side software changes.
Real-time movement ledger: continuous, centralized spatial time-series as both an operational feed and a training dataset for Physical AI.
Protocol-agnostic positioning across 5G, WiFi, LoRa and private cellular with claims of very low bandwidth footprint (e.g., operating on 10–20 MHz) and long read ranges (up to ~1.5 km).
Network-side offload model: position/motion inference executed in the carrier/RAN/central engine to eliminate device battery/compute impact and bypass handset permissions.
